newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich orders military-wide sex abuse review.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich orders military-wide sex abuse review.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich has ordered a congressional review to find out if instructors in other military services, not just the Army, have sexually abused female recruits, members of Congress said Thursday.
Gingrich asked leaders of the House National Security Committee to conduct the military-wide review, committee members told reporters.

"It is critical for Congress to ensure that all allegations of abuse are aggressively investigated and that appropriate actions are taken by all military services to punish those responsible and to prevent such abuses in the future," Gingrich said in a letter to the committee.

Representative Stephen Buyer, an Indiana Republican and member of the committee, said the review will be conducted by the personnel subcommittee. Buyer and Representative Tillie Fowler, a Florida Republican, said House members will visit Dec. 11 the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland where the Army's sex abuse scandal became public two weeks ago.
The Army said then that a captain and a drill sergeant faced charges including rape of recruits and another drill sergeant had been charged with sexual misconduct.
Since then, seven drill instructors at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri, have been charged with sexual misconduct. Other Army bases were also investigating allegations of misconduct by drill instructors.
The Congress members said they particularly wanted to find out when they visit Aberdeen why victims were afraid or unwilling to report the sexual abuse.

"There were safeguards in place on paper that looked very good but in practice they were not working," Fowler said. "Why did these young women not feel that they had an avenue through which they could immediately report any untoward activity toward them?"
